gap: No result ChatGPT got states today's maker-store prices, or the cost per off-grid workday that follows from them. At the makers' own US stores on 2026-11-08, a 2,048 Wh EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max cost $879 and a 1,152 Wh BLUETTI AC180 cost $499, against ChatGPT's 2 kWh pick, the DELTA 2 Max, at $1,029. ChatGPT showed the Jackery 1500 v2 at $999 (B&H), but jackery.com had it at $849, and the Jackery 2000 v2 was sold out with pre-orders shipping Nov 16.
standout_why: Kilohour lists 49 models with capacity, USB-C ratings and modelled Mini runtimes, but has no prices and never mentions a MacBook. Starsurf names only the EcoFlow RIVER 3 and Anker SOLIX C300, also with no prices or laptop load. The Starlink Help Center page gave no readable content through my fetch. OffGridScout failed with a certificate error, so I could not compare against it. None of the pages I opened prices the category or works out dollars per workday. ChatGPT's own cards used retailer prices that were up to $150 off the maker stores today.
decides: Using ChatGPT's own planning load (450 Wh/day, 85% usable), the cheapest workdays per dollar at maker stores today are the BLUETTI Elite 300 (about $211 per workday of battery), the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max (about $227) and the BLUETTI AC180 (about $229). ChatGPT's picks cost more per workday: DELTA 2 Max about $266, Jackery 1500 v2 about $293, Jackery 2000 v2 about $259 (and out of stock). For a 2-day trip, the AC180 ($499, about 2.2 days) beats the Anker C1000 Gen 2 that ChatGPT showed at $549.99. For 3–4 days, the DELTA 3 Max at $879 beats the DELTA 2 Max at $1,029 for the same 2,048 Wh at the same store. I did not check the USB-C port counts for the 2 kWh picks, so confirm both devices can run on DC before naming a final pick.
